back-squat.name: Back squat
back-squat.why: the single biggest builder of leg strength. Trains quads, glutes and trunk under load in the knee-and-hip pattern behind running, jumping, stairs and pedalling.
back-squat.how: bar on upper traps, feet shoulder width, toes slightly out. Big breath, brace, sit down between the hips keeping the chest up and knees tracking over the toes. Depth: thighs at least parallel. Drive the floor away, exhale at the top.
back-squat.cues: "spread the floor", "chest up, elbows under", knees out over the little toe.

trap-bar-deadlift.name: Trap-bar deadlift
trap-bar-deadlift.why: heavy hip-and-knee extension with less lower-back stress than a straight bar. Builds the glutes, hamstrings and grip that lift anything heavy off the floor.
trap-bar-deadlift.how: stand in the middle of the bar, feet hip width. Hinge and grab the high handles, shins near vertical, back flat, chest proud. Push the floor away and stand tall; hips and shoulders rise together. Lower under control, reset every rep.
trap-bar-deadlift.cues: "push, don't pull", "long spine", squeeze the glutes at the top, don't lean back.

romanian-deadlift-rdl.name: Romanian deadlift (RDL)
romanian-deadlift-rdl.why: hamstring and glute strength through the hip hinge; protects the lower back when you bend, lift or hold a forward-leaning position.
romanian-deadlift-rdl.how: bar at the hips, soft knees. Push the hips back and let the bar slide down the thighs, back flat, until you feel a strong hamstring stretch (bar around mid-shin). Drive the hips forward to stand. Knees stay slightly bent the whole time.
romanian-deadlift-rdl.cues: "hips to the wall behind you", bar close to the legs, shoulders down and back.

barbell-hip-thrust.name: Barbell hip thrust
barbell-hip-thrust.why: maximal glute loading with no spinal compression. Strong glutes power sprinting, jumping and standing up from low positions.
barbell-hip-thrust.how: upper back on a bench, bar padded over the hips, feet flat so the shins are vertical at the top. Drive through the heels to full hip extension, chin tucked, ribs down. Pause one second at the top, lower without touching down.
barbell-hip-thrust.cues: "ribs down, chin down", squeeze glutes not lower back, shins vertical at the top.

bulgarian-split-squat.name: Bulgarian split squat
bulgarian-split-squat.why: single-leg strength and stability, which is how you run, climb stairs and pedal. Exposes left/right imbalances.
bulgarian-split-squat.how: rear foot on a bench, front foot far enough forward that the front shin is vertical at the bottom. Dumbbells at the sides. Lower straight down until the rear knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through the front foot.
bulgarian-split-squat.cues: torso slightly forward for glutes, upright for quads; front knee tracks over toes.

dumbbell-step-up.name: Dumbbell step-up
dumbbell-step-up.why: concentric-only single-leg drive from a dead stop, like climbing a steep step.
dumbbell-step-up.how: box at knee height, dumbbells at the sides. Place the whole foot on the box, drive through it to stand fully tall without pushing off the back foot. Step down slowly.
dumbbell-step-up.cues: "no cheating with the back leg", pause at the top, control the descent.

single-leg-leg-press.name: Single-leg leg press
single-leg-leg-press.why: heavy unilateral quad loading with the back supported. Used in later blocks when fatigue from free weights needs to be managed.
single-leg-leg-press.how: one foot mid-platform, hip width. Lower until the knee is at 90° or slightly below, keep the hips down on the pad, press through the whole foot. Don't lock out hard.
single-leg-leg-press.cues: hips stay glued to the seat, knee tracks over toes.

pull-up-weighted.name: Pull-up (weighted)
pull-up-weighted.why: upper-back and grip strength, and posture. Adding load keeps the pull-up progressing once bodyweight reps come easily.
pull-up-weighted.how: overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders, dead hang. Pull the elbows down to the ribs until the chin clears the bar, lower fully under control. Add load with a dip belt or a dumbbell held between the feet.
pull-up-weighted.cues: "elbows to the back pockets", no kipping, full range every rep.

band-assisted-pull-up.name: Band-assisted pull-up
band-assisted-pull-up.why: the first rung of the pull-up ladder. The band carries the share of your bodyweight you cannot lift yet, so you train the full range with real reps instead of failing at two.
band-assisted-pull-up.how: loop a long band over the bar and thread it through itself, then put one knee or both feet in the bottom loop. Same overhand grip as a pull-up, dead hang, pull the elbows down until the chin clears the bar, lower all the way. Move to a thinner band as the reps get easy — the band helps most at the bottom, which is exactly where a beginner stalls.
band-assisted-pull-up.cues: "elbows to the back pockets", keep tension on the band at the top, no kipping.

pull-up-negative.name: Pull-up negative
pull-up-negative.why: the same job as the band-assisted pull-up when there are no bands. You are stronger lowering than lifting, so the eccentric builds the lats, elbows and grip that a full pull-up needs while you still cannot pull yourself up.
pull-up-negative.how: step or jump to the top, chin over the bar, chest up, shoulders set. Take the feet off the box and lower as slowly as you can — aim for 5 seconds — under control the whole way to a dead hang. Step back up to start the next rep. Never drop off the bar.
pull-up-negative.cues: "fight it all the way down", shoulder blades stay down, end the set when a lower gets faster than 3 seconds.

dumbbell-bench-press.name: Dumbbell bench press
dumbbell-bench-press.why: horizontal pressing strength for the chest, shoulders and triceps. Dumbbells are shoulder-friendlier than a barbell.
dumbbell-bench-press.how: flat bench, feet planted, shoulder blades pulled back and down. Lower the dumbbells to chest level with elbows about 45° from the body, press up and slightly in.
dumbbell-bench-press.cues: "bend the bar", squeeze the bench with the shoulder blades, feet drive.

single-arm-dumbbell-row.name: Single-arm dumbbell row
single-arm-dumbbell-row.why: lats and mid-back plus anti-rotation for the trunk. Balances all the pressing.
single-arm-dumbbell-row.how: one hand and knee on a bench (or a staggered stance), back flat. Row the dumbbell to the hip, elbow close to the body, pause, lower fully.
single-arm-dumbbell-row.cues: "pull to the hip, not the armpit", hips level, no torso twist.

landmine-press-single-arm.name: Landmine press (single arm)
landmine-press-single-arm.why: shoulder-safe pressing with a strong core component; the upward arc suits anyone with tight overhead range.
landmine-press-single-arm.how: bar in a landmine or a corner. Half-kneeling or standing, hold the end at the shoulder, brace, press up and forward until the arm is straight. Lower with control.
landmine-press-single-arm.cues: ribs down, glutes tight, don't lean back.
landmine-press-single-arm.loadHint: plates loaded on the bar end

pallof-press.name: Pallof press
pallof-press.why: anti-rotation. Walking, running, carrying and pedalling all try to twist the trunk; this trains you to resist it so force goes where you aim it.
pallof-press.how: cable at chest height, stand side-on, hands together at the sternum. Press the handle straight out and hold 2 seconds, resisting the pull to rotate. Return.
pallof-press.cues: hips and shoulders square, knees soft, breathe.

dead-bug.name: Dead bug
dead-bug.why: anti-extension with hip flexor and trunk coordination, the pattern of holding a stable pelvis while the arms and legs move.
dead-bug.how: on your back, arms up, knees over hips at 90°. Flatten the lower back into the floor. Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor, exhale, return. Alternate.
dead-bug.cues: "lower back never leaves the floor", slow, exhale on the reach.

side-plank.name: Side plank
side-plank.why: lateral trunk and hip stability; the muscles that stop the hips dropping or rocking.
side-plank.how: elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked, lift the hips so the body is a straight line. Hold. Progress with the top leg raised or feet on a bench.
side-plank.cues: "push the floor away", hips forward, don't sag.

front-plank.name: Front plank
front-plank.why: anti-extension endurance. A trunk that holds its shape keeps the lower back from sagging and passes force from the legs to the upper body.
front-plank.how: elbows under the shoulders, forearms flat, feet hip width. Squeeze the glutes, tuck the pelvis so the lower back flattens, and hold a straight line from heel to head. Breathe normally throughout. Stop the moment the hips sag or hike.
front-plank.cues: "ribs down, glutes on", push the floor away, hold a line not a tent.

hanging-knee-raise.name: Hanging knee raise
hanging-knee-raise.why: hip flexor and lower-abdominal strength for the upstroke and grip endurance.
hanging-knee-raise.how: dead hang from a bar. Brace, then lift the knees to hip height or higher without swinging. Lower slowly.
hanging-knee-raise.cues: "tuck the pelvis first", no momentum, 2-second lower.

45-back-extension.name: 45° back extension
45-back-extension.why: posterior chain endurance and glute/hamstring strength for the road position.
45-back-extension.how: pad just below the hip bones. Lower with a flat back to about 90° at the hips, then squeeze the glutes to come back up in line with the legs. Don't hyperextend.
45-back-extension.cues: "glutes, not lower back", stop in a straight line at the top.

farmers-carry.name: Farmer's carry
farmers-carry.why: total-body bracing under load plus grip; trains a rigid trunk while the legs move.
farmers-carry.how: heavy dumbbells or handles, stand tall, shoulders down, walk with short quick steps for the set distance. Set down with a hinge.
farmers-carry.cues: "walk like you're proud", no leaning, breathe behind the brace.

box-jump.name: Box jump
box-jump.why: rate of force development with a soft landing. Teaches maximal intent, which is what turns strength into speed and power.
box-jump.how: stand a short step from a box you can land on with a quarter-squat, not a deep crouch. Swing the arms back, dip, and drive up onto the box. Land softly, stand tall, then step (never jump) down.
box-jump.cues: "land quiet", full hip extension in the air, reset between every jump.

standing-broad-jump.name: Standing broad jump
standing-broad-jump.why: horizontal power test and training tool. We use it as the W1 baseline and re-test.
standing-broad-jump.how: feet shoulder width behind a line. Swing arms back with a hip hinge, then drive arms forward and up and jump for distance. Land on both feet and stick it. Measure heel.
standing-broad-jump.cues: "arms lead", full extension, stick the landing or the jump doesn't count.

trap-bar-jump.name: Trap-bar jump
trap-bar-jump.why: loaded jump without a bar on the spine. Builds explosive hip and knee extension for sprinting and jumping.
trap-bar-jump.how: trap bar with light load (20–30% of your deadlift). Set up as for a deadlift, then jump as high as possible, land soft with the bar under control, reset fully before the next.
trap-bar-jump.cues: "jump, don't lift", hips through, quiet landing.

kettlebell-swing.name: Kettlebell swing
kettlebell-swing.why: repeated explosive hip extension; power endurance for the posterior chain.
kettlebell-swing.how: hinge, hike the bell back between the legs, then snap the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms are ropes. Let it fall and hinge again.
kettlebell-swing.cues: "it's a hinge, not a squat", stand up hard, glutes finish the swing.

hang-power-clean.name: Hang power clean
hang-power-clean.why: the highest power-output lift in the gym. Used only in the power block, once technique is clean.
hang-power-clean.how: bar at the hips, hinge to just above the knees. Explode the hips forward, shrug, pull the elbows high and fast, and catch the bar on the shoulders in a quarter squat. Stand up. Lower to the hips and repeat.
hang-power-clean.cues: "jump and catch", elbows fast, bar stays close.

goblet-squat.name: Goblet squat
goblet-squat.why: teaches the squat pattern with the load held in front, which keeps the chest up and the depth honest. Builds the quads and glutes with very little that can go wrong.
goblet-squat.how: hold one dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against the chest, elbows under it. Feet a little wider than hips, toes slightly out. Sit down between the heels, knees tracking over the toes, until the elbows brush the inside of the knees. Stand up through the whole foot.
goblet-squat.cues: "elbows inside the knees", chest proud, heels stay down.

leg-press.name: Leg press
leg-press.why: heavy leg work with the back supported, so the quads and glutes can be loaded while balance and bracing are not the limit.
leg-press.how: sit with the lower back flat against the pad, feet hip width in the middle of the platform. Release the handles, lower until the knees reach about 90° without the hips rolling off the pad, then press through the whole foot. Stop just short of locking the knees.
leg-press.cues: hips stay glued to the seat, knees follow the toes, smooth down and up.

dumbbell-reverse-lunge.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
dumbbell-reverse-lunge.why: single-leg strength with a gentler knee angle than a forward lunge. A long step back and a slight forward lean put the work into the glutes.
dumbbell-reverse-lunge.how: stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand. Take a long step back, lower until the back knee is just above the floor with the front shin close to vertical, then drive through the front heel to return. Finish all reps on one side, then switch.
dumbbell-reverse-lunge.cues: "step long, drop straight down", front knee over the middle of the foot.

dumbbell-romanian-deadlift.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
dumbbell-romanian-deadlift.why: the hip hinge with dumbbells: hamstrings and glutes through a long range, and the pattern that protects the back when lifting anything off the floor.
dumbbell-romanian-deadlift.how: dumbbells in front of the thighs, soft knees. Push the hips back and slide the dumbbells down the legs with a flat back until the hamstrings are stretched, about mid-shin. Squeeze the glutes to drive the hips forward and stand tall.
dumbbell-romanian-deadlift.cues: "hips to the wall behind you", dumbbells brush the legs, neck long.

glute-bridge.name: Glute bridge
glute-bridge.why: direct glute work from the floor, the easiest way to learn to finish a hip extension with the glutes rather than the lower back.
glute-bridge.how: lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width, a dumbbell or plate resting on the hips. Tuck the ribs down, press through the heels and lift the hips until the body is a straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze for a second, lower slowly.
glute-bridge.cues: "ribs down, squeeze and hold", push through the heels, no arching.

leg-curl.name: Leg curl
leg-curl.why: hamstring strength at the knee, which balances all the squatting and pressing work on the front of the leg.
leg-curl.how: set the machine so the knees line up with its pivot and the pad sits just above the heels. Curl the heels towards the glutes, pause, and lower under control until the legs are almost straight.
leg-curl.cues: hips stay down on the pad, slow on the way back, no swinging.

cable-glute-kickback.name: Cable glute kickback
cable-glute-kickback.why: isolates the glute on one side at a time, a good finisher once the big lifts are done.
cable-glute-kickback.how: ankle strap on a low cable. Face the stack, hold the frame, soft standing knee. Kick the strapped leg straight back until the glute is fully squeezed, without arching the lower back, then return slowly. Finish one side, then switch.
cable-glute-kickback.cues: "move the leg, not the back", pause at the top, hips square.

hip-abduction.name: Hip abduction
hip-abduction.why: trains the side glutes that keep the knees tracking well in squats, lunges and step-ups.
hip-abduction.how: on the seated machine, sit tall with the pads outside the knees and press the knees apart as far as they comfortably go, pause, and return slowly. On a cable, stand side-on with an ankle strap on the far leg and lift it out to the side.
hip-abduction.cues: slow on the way in, pause out wide, torso still.

dead-hang.name: Dead hang
dead-hang.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
dead-hang.why: grip and shoulder strength for everything that happens on a bar. The first rung of the pull-up path: a pull-up starts from a hang you can hold.
dead-hang.how: grab the bar overhand, shoulder width, and lift the feet so you hang with straight arms. Keep the shoulders slightly active, pulled away from the ears, and breathe. Step down before the grip opens.
dead-hang.cues: "shoulders away from the ears", squeeze the bar, legs still.

scapular-pull-up.name: Scapular pull-up
scapular-pull-up.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
scapular-pull-up.why: teaches the first few centimetres of a pull-up, pulling the shoulder blades down before the arms bend, which is the part most people skip.
scapular-pull-up.how: from a dead hang, keep the arms straight and pull the shoulder blades down and together so the body rises a few centimetres. Hold for a second, then lower back to the hang under control.
scapular-pull-up.cues: "arms stay straight", chest lifts towards the bar, no bending at the elbows.

pull-up.name: Pull-up
pull-up.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
pull-up.why: the strict bodyweight pull-up: a real measure of upper-body pulling strength.
pull-up.how: overhand grip slightly wider than the shoulders, start from a dead hang. Pull the shoulder blades down, then the elbows down to the ribs until the chin clears the bar. Lower all the way to straight arms. No kicking or swinging.
pull-up.cues: "shoulder blades first", elbows to the back pockets, full hang between reps.

lat-pulldown.name: Lat pulldown
lat-pulldown.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
lat-pulldown.why: builds the same pulling muscles as a pull-up with a load lighter than bodyweight, so it adds volume on the way to the first pull-up.
lat-pulldown.how: sit with the thighs under the pad, hands slightly wider than shoulder width. Lean back a little, pull the bar to the upper chest by driving the elbows down, pause, and let it rise until the arms are straight.
lat-pulldown.cues: "elbows to the back pockets", chest up to the bar, no yanking.

inverted-row.name: Inverted row
inverted-row.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
inverted-row.why: a horizontal bodyweight pull for the upper back that is easy to scale by changing the bar height or the foot position.
inverted-row.how: set a bar at about waist height in a rack or Smith machine. Hang underneath with straight arms, heels on the floor, body in a straight line. Pull the chest to the bar, pause, lower slowly. Lower the bar to make it harder.
inverted-row.cues: body stays a plank, squeeze the shoulder blades together, chest to the bar.

incline-push-up.name: Incline push-up
incline-push-up.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
incline-push-up.why: the push-up pattern with less of the body to press, so every rep can be full range while strength builds.
incline-push-up.how: hands on a bench, box or bar a little wider than the shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels. Lower the chest to the edge with the elbows about 45° from the body, then press away. Lower the surface as the reps get easy.
incline-push-up.cues: "one straight line", elbows back not out, chest touches first.

push-up.name: Push-up
push-up.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
push-up.why: pressing strength for the chest, shoulders and arms, with the trunk working to hold the body straight.
push-up.how: hands a little wider than the shoulders, body in a straight line, feet together. Lower until the chest is just above the floor with the elbows about 45° from the body, then press the floor away. Go back to an incline for the last reps if the hips sag.
push-up.cues: "squeeze the glutes, brace the belly", elbows back, full range.

dumbbell-shoulder-press.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
dumbbell-shoulder-press.group: Upper body — the pull-up path and pushing
dumbbell-shoulder-press.why: overhead pressing strength for the shoulders and arms, with the trunk braced.
dumbbell-shoulder-press.how: seated with back support, or standing with glutes tight. Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward or slightly in. Press up until the arms are straight overhead, then lower to the shoulders under control.
dumbbell-shoulder-press.cues: ribs down, no leaning back, wrists stacked over the elbows.

bird-dog.name: Bird dog
bird-dog.why: trunk control and balance: the back stays still while an arm and the opposite leg move, which is the same job the core does in every lift.
bird-dog.how: on hands and knees, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with the body, hold two seconds, return. Alternate sides.
bird-dog.cues: "don't spill the water on your back", slow, hips stay square.
